mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has risen monotonically from -52.3 to -45.0 over four weeks while RETAIL_REC stayed flat near -35.5. The released trip capacity is currently absorbed by commuting and errands; within four weeks it spills into discretionary trips that lift RETAIL_REC above its last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -52.3 at t-3w to -45.0 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC moved only from -37.4 to -35.3
failure_condition: TRANSIT continues rising above -45 in the next four weeks while the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below -35.5.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of RESIDENTIAL falling from 12.7 to 10.1 and PARKS jumping to 42.6 shows households reallocating time out of the home. Because that reallocation is broader than parks alone, it carries households past retail corridors, raising RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 12.7 at t-3w to 10.1 at t-0w while PARKS rose from 17.3 to 42.6
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL keeps falling and PARKS stays above +30 for two weeks, yet RETAIL_REC's next-14-day mean is below its previous-14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A transit crossing above -46 marks the point where non-commute trips restart in volume; the observed move from -48.0 to -45.0 satisfies this crossing and, sustained, pulls WORKPLACES up and RETAIL_REC up over a two-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean crosses above -46 and posts a further week-on-week gain
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT crossed from -48.0 at t-1w to -45.0 at t-0w and WORKPLACES rose from -42.7 to -39.3
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -46 and gains again, but RETAIL_REC over the following 14 days is not higher than over the preceding 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime defined by RESIDENTIAL dropping below 11.0 while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES climb, capacity limits on indoor commerce are eased and previously suppressed retail demand is released, lifting RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below 11.0 while TRANSIT rises for a third consecutive week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell to 10.1 at t-0w, TRANSIT rose to -45.0 and WORKPLACES rose to -39.3
regime_hint: active reopening with declining stay-at-home share
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below 11.0 with TRANSIT rising for three weeks, but RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is lower than its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The one-week PARKS jump of 18.6 points to 42.6 marks the late-summer outdoor peak. As autumn shortens outdoor daylight hours, that leisure time is displaced indoors toward retail and grocery venues, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds +30 and then decelerates in week-on-week change
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 24.0 at t-1w to 42.6 at t-0w, its largest weekly increase in the snapshot
failure_condition: After PARKS exceeds +30 and its weekly change decelerates, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not above its last-28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The PARKS surge to 42.6 combined with falling RESIDENTIAL shows discretionary hours being spent on free outdoor activity rather than indoor commerce. While PARKS stays above +40, that substitution crowds out retail trips and drives RETAIL_REC down over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean remains above +40 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 42.6 while RESIDENTIAL fell to 10.1 at t-0w
regime_hint: reopening with strong outdoor leisure demand
failure_condition: PARKS stays above +40 for two consecutive weeks yet RETAIL_REC's next-14-day mean exceeds its previous-14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The mobility recovery is commute-driven: TRANSIT gains are matched by WORKPLACES gains while RETAIL_REC stays below -34, so the next week of transit expansion adds work trips only. With no discretionary-trip conversion, RETAIL_REC drifts lower over one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean exceeds -44 while RETAIL_REC remains below -34
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 7.3 points over four weeks while RETAIL_REC improved only 2.1 points and stayed negative
failure_condition: TRANSIT exceeds -44 with RETAIL_REC below -34, but the following week's RETAIL_REC mean is above the t-0w value of -35.3.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -22.3 at t-3w to -15.0 at t-0w, a 7.3 point gain
